title: Maximum Score After Splitting a String
statement: The string `s` holds only the characters `'0'` and `'1'`. Cut it at one position into a left part and a right part, both non-empty. The score of a cut is how many `'0'` characters the left part has plus how many `'1'` characters the right part has. Return the highest score over all possible cuts.
constraints: s contains only the characters '0' and '1'
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every cut and recounting both parts works but costs O(n²). Moving the cut one step right moves exactly one character from the right part to the left part, so the two counts change by at most one. Start with the total number of ones (all in the right part), then sweep the cut from left to right, keeping a running count of zeros on the left and ones on the right: a prefix sum maintained on the fly.

## Approach

1. Count all `'1'` characters into `onesRight`: before any cut, everything is on the right.
2. Set `zerosLeft = 0` and `best = 0`.
3. For each `i` from `0` to `s.length - 2`, move `s[i]` to the left part: a `'0'` increases `zerosLeft`, a `'1'` decreases `onesRight`.
4. The cut now sits just after `i`; update `best` with `zerosLeft + onesRight`.
5. Return `best`. The loop stops before the last character so the right part is never empty.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "011101"` has four ones, so `onesRight = 4`.

| `i` | `s[i]` | `zerosLeft` | `onesRight` | score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 1 | 4 | 5 |
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 3 | 4 |
| 2 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| 4 | 0 | 2 | 1 | 3 |

The best score is `5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to count ones and one pass over the cuts.
- Space: O(1): only a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- Both parts must be non-empty, so the cut index stops at `s.length - 2`; including the last position would allow an empty right part and can overcount (for `"00"` the answer is 1, not 2).
- When the left part grows by a `'1'`, the right part loses that one; forgetting to decrement `onesRight` inflates every later score.
- A string of all `'1'` characters still has positive answers (`"1111"` scores 3), so do not special-case it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ch` | a character of `s` during the first counting pass |
| `onesRight` | number of `'1'` characters in the right part |
| `zerosLeft` | number of `'0'` characters in the left part |
| `best` | highest score seen over the cuts so far |
| `i` | index of the last character in the left part |
